cas: Deleting an ingredient by a name that differs from the stored name only in upper/lower case (« farine » vs « Farine »): the spec does not say whether this deletes the ingredient or does nothing.
verdict:
claim:     When `remove_ingredient(Omelette#1, 'farine')` is called on a recipe that holds the ingredient « Farine », the spec settles whether that ingredient must disappear.
ruling:    rejected
because:   A04 says « La suppression d'un ingrédient le fait disparaître de la liste des ingrédients de la recette ». That assumes the deleted ingredient has already been identified. Nothing in the spec says a name with different capitals points to that ingredient. The only rule about upper and lower case is A17, « Une requête en majuscules donne les mêmes résultats que la même requête en minuscules », and it covers search requests, not editing a recipe. So reading 'farine' as « Farine » (Y's behaviour) and treating it as an ingredient that isn't there (X's behaviour) both fit the spec.
certainty: close. A user would probably expect 'farine' to mean « Farine », but no assertion says so. Only the arbiter can say whether A17's case rule was meant to apply to ingredient names too.

CLASSE: trou
ASSERTION: A04
CAS: Deleting an ingredient by a name that differs from the stored name only in upper/lower case (« farine » vs « Farine »): the spec does not say whether this deletes the ingredient or does nothing.
